title: Object pronouns
objectives: I can tell a direct object from an indirect object and replace nouns with me, te, nos, o, a, os, as, lhe and lhes.
I can use everyday Brazilian patterns such as te amo, me liga, vi ele and short answers with no pronoun at all.
I can place pronouns correctly before the verb in speech, and recognize the hyphenated formal pattern in writing.
I can use pronouns after prepositions, including comigo, com você, para mim and para eu, and use dar with indirect pronouns.

vocabulary.note: Irregular: eu dou, ele dá, nós damos, eles dão; preterite dei, deu, demos, deram.

example.pt: Meu pai me deu este relógio.
example.en: My father gave me this watch.

example.pt: Você pode me emprestar o carregador?
example.en: Can you lend me the charger?

vocabulary.note: Also means to order someone to do something.

example.pt: Mandei uma mensagem para ela ontem.
example.en: I sent her a message yesterday.

example.pt: Vou entregar o pedido hoje à tarde.
example.en: I am going to deliver the order this afternoon.

example.pt: Preciso devolver o livro à biblioteca.
example.en: I need to return the book to the library.

example.pt: Recebi a sua mensagem agora.
example.en: I just received your message.

vocabulary.note: Also means to turn on. Ligar para alguém and ligar alguém are both heard; in speech people say te ligar.

example.pt: Vou te ligar mais tarde.
example.en: I will call you later.

example.pt: Me avisa se você vai atrasar.
example.en: Let me know if you are going to be late.

example.pt: Ele me contou uma novidade incrível.
example.en: He told me incredible news.

vocabulary.note: The person asked is an indirect object: perguntar a alguém, or me perguntou.

example.pt: Vou perguntar para ela onde fica o banco.
example.en: I will ask her where the bank is.

vocabulary.note: In Portuguese the person is an indirect object: ele me respondeu.

example.pt: Ela ainda não me respondeu.
example.en: She has not answered me yet.

example.pt: Vou convidar vocês para o meu aniversário.
example.en: I am going to invite you all to my birthday.

example.pt: Posso te apresentar a minha amiga?
example.en: May I introduce you to my friend?

vocabulary.note: The person thanked is an indirect object: agradecer a alguém, or te agradeço.

example.pt: Quero agradecer a vocês pela ajuda.
example.en: I want to thank you all for the help.

example.pt: Minha tia me ensinou a cozinhar.
example.en: My aunt taught me to cook.

vocabulary.note: Te amo is used warmly for family, partners and close friends.

example.pt: Eu te amo muito.
example.en: I love you very much.

example.pt: Eu confio em você.
example.en: I trust you.

vocabulary.note: Also estar com saudade de. Saudade has no single English equivalent.

example.pt: Sinto saudade de você.
example.en: I miss you.

example.pt: Comprei um presente para você.
example.en: I bought a gift for you.

example.pt: Isso é um segredo entre mim e você.
example.en: This is a secret between you and me.

example.pt: Tenho uma novidade para te contar.
example.en: I have some news to tell you.

example.pt: O caixa me deu o troco errado.
example.en: The cashier gave me the wrong change.

vocabulary.note: Nota fiscal is the official invoice or sales receipt.

example.pt: Pode me dar o recibo, por favor?
example.en: Can you give me the receipt, please?

example.pt: A encomenda chegou hoje de manhã.
example.en: The parcel arrived this morning.

example.pt: Ela me apresentou o namorado dela.
example.en: She introduced her boyfriend to me.

dialogues.title: Picking up an order
dialogues.context: Rodrigo bought a backpack online and comes to the store to pick it up. Patrícia, the attendant, helps him.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Boa tarde! Em que posso te ajudar?
lines.en: Good afternoon! How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Boa tarde. Comprei uma mochila pela internet. Vocês me mandaram uma mensagem ontem.
lines.en: Good afternoon. I bought a backpack online. You sent me a message yesterday.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Qual é o seu nome, por favor?
lines.en: What is your name, please?

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Rodrigo Alves.
lines.en: Rodrigo Alves.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Um momento, vou procurar a sua encomenda. Achei! Aqui está.
lines.en: One moment, I will look for your order. Found it! Here it is.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Obrigado! Pode me dar o recibo também?
lines.en: Thank you! Can you give me the receipt too?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Posso, sim. Vou te entregar agora. Você pagou cem reais, certo?
lines.en: Yes, I can. I will hand it to you now. You paid one hundred reais, right?

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Paguei. A mochila custa oitenta e cinco, mas vocês me deram só dez de troco.
lines.en: I did. The backpack costs eighty-five, but you only gave me ten in change.

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Desculpa! Eu te dei o troco errado. Aqui estão mais cinco reais.
lines.en: Sorry! I gave you the wrong change. Here are five more reais.

lines.speaker: Rodrigo
lines.pt: Tudo bem. E se eu não gostar, dá pra trocar?
lines.en: That is fine. And if I do not like it, can I exchange it?

lines.speaker: Patrícia
lines.pt: Dá, sim. Você tem sete dias. É só me trazer a mochila com o recibo.
lines.en: Yes, you can. You have seven days. Just bring me the backpack with the receipt.

dialogues.title: Big news
dialogues.context: Carol has some news and tells her friend Bruno over coffee.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: Bruno, tenho uma novidade pra te contar.
lines.en: Bruno, I have some news to tell you.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Me conta! Estou curioso.
lines.en: Tell me! I am curious.

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: O Felipe me convidou pra morar com ele.
lines.en: Felipe invited me to move in with him.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Sério? Você já respondeu pra ele?
lines.en: Really? Have you answered him already?

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: Ainda não. Vou pensar. Eu vi ele ontem, mas não falei nada.
lines.en: Not yet. I will think about it. I saw him yesterday, but I did not say anything.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Você ama ele?
lines.en: Do you love him?

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: Amo. E confio nele também. Mas é uma decisão grande.
lines.en: I do. And I trust him too. But it is a big decision.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Então diz pra ele que sim! Já apresentou ele pra sua mãe?
lines.en: Then tell him yes! Have you introduced him to your mother yet?

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: Apresentei. Ela gostou muito dele.
lines.en: I have. She liked him a lot.

lines.speaker: Bruno
lines.pt: Viu? Quer conversar comigo depois do jantar?
lines.en: See? Do you want to talk with me after dinner?

lines.speaker: Carol
lines.pt: Quero. Obrigada, Bruno. Sinto saudade de conversar com você.
lines.en: I do. Thanks, Bruno. I miss talking with you.

dialogues.title: Borrowing a tent
dialogues.context: Diego is going camping and calls his friend Mariana to borrow some equipment.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Oi, Mari! Preciso de um favor. Você pode me emprestar a sua barraca?
lines.en: Hi, Mari! I need a favor. Can you lend me your tent?

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.pt: Claro! Pra onde você vai?
lines.en: Of course! Where are you going?

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Vou acampar na serra com a Júlia e o Caio. Por que você não vem com a gente?
lines.en: I am going camping in the mountains with Júlia and Caio. Why don't you come with us?

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.pt: Eu adoraria, mas tenho trabalho no sábado. Quem sabe eu encontro vocês no domingo.
lines.en: I would love to, but I have work on Saturday. Maybe I will meet you on Sunday.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Boa! Vou te mandar o endereço do lugar. E a lanterna, você me empresta também?
lines.en: Great! I will send you the address of the place. And the flashlight, will you lend me that too?

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.pt: Empresto. Vou deixar tudo na portaria pra você. Passa lá de tarde.
lines.en: I will. I will leave everything at the front desk for you. Stop by in the afternoon.

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Valeu! Eu te devolvo tudo na segunda, prometo.
lines.en: Thanks! I will give it all back to you on Monday, I promise.

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.pt: Tá bom. Me manda uma foto da barraca armada!
lines.en: Okay. Send me a photo of the tent set up!

lines.speaker: Diego
lines.pt: Mando! Um beijo pra você.
lines.en: I will! A kiss for you.

lines.speaker: Mariana
lines.pt: Divirta-se! Um beijo pra Júlia também.
lines.en: Have fun! A kiss for Júlia too.

grammar.title: Direct and indirect object pronouns
grammar.explanation:
A direct object answers the question who or what, with no preposition: Eu vejo a Ana. An indirect object answers to whom or for whom, usually with a or para: Eu dei o livro à Ana. Pronouns replace both. Me, te and nos work as direct and indirect objects: Ela me viu (saw me) and Ela me deu um livro (gave to me). The third person differs: o, a, os, as are direct objects (him, her, them), and lhe and lhes are indirect objects (to him, to her, to them, to you formal).

Several Portuguese verbs take an indirect object where English uses a direct one: responder (ele me respondeu, he answered me), perguntar (perguntei a ele), agradecer (agradeço a vocês) and telefonar. Dar, mandar, emprestar, contar, ensinar and entregar take both: a thing (direct) and a person (indirect), as in Ela me contou a novidade.

In Brazilian speech, te is the standard object pronoun for você (Eu te amo, Posso te ajudar?), even though você itself is grammatically third person. O, a, os and as are mostly written; lhe and lhes sound formal and are heard mainly in service language, letters and contracts.

examples.en: She called me last night.

examples.pt: Meu pai me deu um relógio.

examples.en: I love you very much.

examples.en: He sent us a message.

grammar.title: Everyday Brazilian patterns: vi ele, te amo, dropped objects
grammar.explanation:
In spoken Brazilian Portuguese, Brazilians put the subject pronouns ele, ela, eles and elas in the direct-object slot: Eu vi ele, Eu convidei elas, Eu conheço eles. Textbooks call this non-standard and recommend o, a, os and as in writing (Eu o vi), but it is universal in conversation, and o and a are now rare outside writing.

Another very common pattern is to drop the object altogether when the context is clear. If someone asks Você comprou o pão?, the natural answer is just Comprei, not Comprei-o. Repeating the noun or using a short answer is far more common than using o and a.

For você as an object, speakers use te even when they say você elsewhere in the sentence: Você sabe que eu te adoro. For a formal customer-service tone, speakers may use o senhor, a senhora or lhe: Posso ajudá-lo? For we as an object, a gente does not change: Ele viu a gente, not Ele nos viu, although nos appears in writing and in fixed phrases.

rows: I invited them to the party.
Did you buy the bread? I did.
Ele viu a gente no shopping.
He saw us at the mall.

examples.pt: Eu vi ela no mercado hoje cedo.
examples.en: I saw her at the market this morning.

examples.pt: Vamos convidar eles para o churrasco?
examples.en: Shall we invite them to the barbecue?

examples.pt: Você viu o filme? Vi, sim.
examples.en: Did you see the movie? Yes, I did.

examples.pt: Eu sempre ajudo ele com o dever de casa.
examples.en: I always help him with his homework.

examples.pt: Posso te ajudar com alguma coisa?
examples.en: Can I help you with anything?

examples.pt: Ele chamou a gente para jantar.
examples.en: He invited us to dinner.

grammar.title: Where the pronoun goes
grammar.explanation:
In Brazilian speech, object pronouns go directly before the verb they belong to: Ela me disse a verdade, Não te vi ontem, Ninguém me avisou. This is also the standard written pattern after a subject or a negative word. Avoid putting a weak pronoun at the start of a formal written sentence; there, the pronoun follows the verb with a hyphen: Diga-me, Avisaram-nos, Deu-me a chave. In conversation, saying Me diz or Me liga at the start of a sentence is perfectly natural.

With ir plus infinitive and with modals such as poder and querer, Brazilians put the pronoun before the infinitive, and this is standard: Vou te ligar, Posso te ajudar?, Quero te contar uma coisa. The old pattern with the hyphen (Vou ligar-te) belongs to European Portuguese and sounds stiff in Brazil.

After verb forms ending in -r, -s or -z, formal writing turns o and a into lo and la and drops the final letter: comprar + o becomes comprá-lo, fazer + o becomes fazê-lo. After a nasal ending, o and a become no and na: compraram-no.

examples.pt: Ela me contou tudo ontem.
examples.en: She told me everything yesterday.

examples.pt: Não te vi na festa.
examples.en: I did not see you at the party.

examples.pt: Vou te mandar o endereço agora.
examples.en: I am going to send you the address now.

examples.pt: Quero te apresentar uma pessoa.
examples.en: I want to introduce you to someone.

examples.pt: Pode me dar o recibo, por favor?
examples.en: Can you give me the receipt, please?

examples.pt: Diga-me o seu nome completo.
examples.en: Tell me your full name.

grammar.title: Pronouns after prepositions, and dar
grammar.explanation:
After a preposition, the pronoun forms are mim for eu and ti for tu; the others are the same as the subject pronouns: para mim, para você, para ele, para nós, para a gente, para vocês. With com, the pronouns fuse: comigo (with me), contigo (with you, only with tu), conosco (with us, formal or written). In everyday speech com você and com a gente are more common than contigo and conosco.

There is one classic trap. When the pronoun is the subject of a following infinitive, use eu, not mim: É difícil para eu entender, Trouxe isso para você ler. Para mim ler is a common error. The form mim stays only when it is not the subject of a verb: Isso é para mim, Entre mim e você.

The verb dar works with the indirect pronouns: Me dá um minuto, Ele te deu o troco?, Ela nos deu uma boa notícia. For the third person, speech normally prefers a prepositional phrase: Dei o presente para ela, Deu o livro pra ele. Lhe is reserved for formal writing and polite service: Dei-lhe o livro.

examples.pt: Esse presente é para mim?
examples.en: Is this gift for me?

examples.pt: Vem comigo ao mercado?
examples.en: Will you come to the market with me?

examples.pt: É difícil para eu acordar cedo.
examples.en: It is hard for me to wake up early.

examples.pt: Me dá um minuto, por favor.
examples.en: Give me a minute, please.

examples.pt: Ela deu o livro pra ele.
examples.en: She gave the book to him.

examples.pt: Vocês querem ir com a gente?
examples.en: Do you want to go with us?

culture.title: Te amo, me liga and the gap between writing and speech
culture.text:
Brazilian Portuguese has an unusually wide gap between what grammar books prescribe and what people say. Eu vi ele, me liga and te amo are heard everywhere, from TV to the university, while eu o vi, ligue-me and amo-te sound stiff or belong to Portugal. Brazilians handle the gap easily: they write a formal email or a legal contract with lhe and the hyphen, and they talk to friends with me and te. A learner who speaks the everyday pattern will be understood and sounds natural, while someone who speaks in textbook forms may sound like a letter.

The pronoun te is the great connector. Even when you address a stranger as você, it is normal to say posso te ajudar? or vou te mandar o endereço. In parts of the South, the North and the Northeast, speakers use tu with contigo and ti as well. Messages between friends are full of these patterns: me avisa quando chegar, te ligo depois and me manda uma foto. The word saudade appears constantly in them, as in Tô com saudade de você, a very warm way to tell someone you miss them.

Match the pronoun with its meaning
In 'Ela me deu um presente', what does 'me' mean?
exercises.explanation: Me is the indirect object here. The direct object is um presente.

exercises.prompt: Which is the most natural everyday way to say 'I saw her yesterday'?
exercises.explanation: Brazilians use ele and ela after the verb in speech. Vi-a is the European Portuguese pattern.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is correct for 'This book is for me to read'?
choices: Este livro é para mim ler.
Este livro é para me ler.
Este livro é para eu ler.
exercises.explanation: When the pronoun is the subject of the infinitive, use eu, not mim.
Com and mim fuse into comigo.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence sounds natural in everyday Brazilian speech?
exercises.explanation: With ir plus infinitive, Brazilians put the pronoun before the infinitive.

exercises.prompt: In formal writing, which pronoun means 'to him' or 'to her'?
exercises.explanation: Lhe is the indirect object pronoun for the third person. In speech, people say para ele or para ela.

exercises.prompt: Which verb takes an indirect object in Portuguese, although 'to answer' takes a direct object in English?
exercises.explanation: Ele me respondeu literally means he answered to me.
